### PROCESSUS LXXVII.
**Tinctura of Tartarized Tartar.**

#### APPARATUS
On Tartarized Tartar <note>potassium tartrate</note>, prepared correctly according to Process 75 and dried, then ground into a fine powder, pour into a tall chemical vial the purest alcohol of wine until it exceeds the powder by four inches. Then, with the vial sealed only with paper, let them boil together as gently as possible in our wooden furnace for the space of a day and a night. The alcohol floating on top will be golden in color, with an aromatic odor and a penetrating, hot taste. If this is repeated with new alcohol in the same manner, a white salt will finally be left at the bottom. The tinctures are thickened over a gentle fire until a tenth part remains concentrated at the bottom.

#### USE
This serves to demonstrate the part in that salt which is dissolved by alcohol. The prepared tincture itself is aromatic, warming, and heals ulcers and wounds. The remaining salt, being simpler than before, shows that salts themselves can be whitened once the tincture is drawn out by the help of alcohol.

### PROCESSUS LXXVIII.
**Dissolution of Regenerated Tartar in Alcohol.**

#### APPARATUS
Upon Regenerated Tartar <note>potassium acetate</note>, previously prepared as neatly as possible and as safely as can be done, in a tall glass chemical vial, pour six times as much of the purest alcohol. Boil it with a gentle fire in our wooden furnace with great care. They will combine with one another, and from these will be made a certain uniformly composed substance, with the dregs deposited at the bottom. Afterward, when they have settled accurately through rest, let the clear, supernatant liquor flow out by a careful tilting of the vessel. If any saline matter not yet dissolved remains, it can be dissolved with the application of fresh alcohol using the same caution, and separated from the dregs. Then, indeed, let the prepared liquors be concentrated to half their volume by distilling with a very gentle fire; thus the Tincture of this salt will be obtained.

#### USE
In this experiment, you see united into one the alkali, the oily acid, and the oily portion of the vegetable spirits. Hence, the most active principles of plants are freed from the inert earth; yet at the same time they are safe enough, and their sharp pungency is no longer dangerous. These indeed, thus united, seem to constitute even the "Lesser Elixir of the Sages" <note>Elixir parvum Sapientum</note>, which the Masters of the Ancient Art recommended for preserving and restoring health. It heals almost all obstacles,

<column-break/>

penetrates through the vessels, and excites life with a pleasant stimulus, so that it heals by perspiration. In chemical matters, it also provides a most effective solvent, by which things are reduced to their smallest, active parts, with their seminal virtue unharmed, so that they can thus be admitted into the innermost recesses of the body to restrain and subdue all rebellious conditions. Nor is it less praised for the beauty of its effects which it provides for external ailments of the body, such as wounds, ulcers, and tumors. Nor should this so healthy remedy be denied to the poor out of ambition; for it can be prepared instantly by mixing potash with fifteen parts of the sharpest vinegar, straining, and thickening: thus without expense of labor or price, it can be prepared and used fit for purpose. This was known to the ancients in Rome. Pliny, Book 23, in the Preface: "The ash of twigs sprinkled with vinegar is drunk for ailments of the spleen."

### PROCESSUS LXXIX.
**Harvey’s Tincture of Salt of Tartar.**

#### APPARATUS
I take the alkaline salt, very black, which remained in the glass retort after all the volatile matter was expelled by distillation from Tartar using the highest heat of a sand bath, according to Process 55. To this, quickly crushed into powder in a hot iron mortar with a hot pestle and placed into a tall glass vial, I pour the best common spirits of wine so that they float four inches above. I boil this in this tall vial over a gentle fire in our wooden furnace for twenty hours. A thin black liquor will be obtained, with a bitter, aromatic, and lye-like taste. Let this be poured off pure. Thus, it can be kept safe for its intended uses in a closed vessel under its own name.

#### USE
Common spirit of wine, consisting of water, acid, and alcohol united, boiling with the alkali of Tartar (which is still oily), makes a gentler and safer lye. This is because the alkali is tempered by the acid, oil, and alcohol; from which a type of medicament and solvent is born that is by no means ignoble. In chemistry, when cooked or digested with vegetables, it performs well by beautifully dissolving simple substances. In surgery, it is a most noble remedy for purifying, cleansing, drying, and healing moist, purulent, putrid, foul, and virulent ulcers, as well as bad sores, whether they are fistulous or deep and spreading like burrows; also for consuming those things which grow out in too much excess; especially if it is mixed skillfully with a little oil.
